notes: Named sim presets the BiS ranker runs a level-60 band under besides the bare character. Every id is in sim/request's vocabulary (buffs and debuffs from the engine's four buff messages, consumables from its Consumes message); a test refuses an unknown one. The class kit (sim/leveling KitBuffs and KitConsumes) is layered on top and wins any consumable slot it holds.

raid.label: Raid-ready, Phase 1
raid.notes: The same Phase 1 raid context for every spec: one group of each class brings its buffs and debuffs, each spec adds the consumables its role uses, no world buffs (Forever has none), the default 180 second encounter. Where a buff has a talented form, the plain version is used unless the live talent tree carries the talent and a raid would take it; only Mana Spring qualifies, through the Restoration shaman's Restorative Totems (watch forever-bugs #215, which asks for that talent's removal: if it goes, the preset goes back to the plain totem). Blessing of Kings is left out. It is learnable (a trainer spell from level 20, SkillLineAbility 20217 and Greater Blessing of Kings 25898), but its +10% to every stat is the same aura and amount as Heart of the Lion's, which this preset already carries, and nothing in the client says whether the two stack (they share no SpellLabel or other exclusivity row); If they do stack, carrying Kings measured about 4% more for Fury and Retribution and about 1.5% for Fire (level-60 raid band, 2026-10-31); a beta character sheet with both buffs settles it. Sanctity Aura is left out too: spell 20218 has no SkillLineAbility row in the Forever client, so no paladin can learn it. Windfury Totem is a raid-buff aura, as in the client (spells 8512 to 10614: an aura on every party member, not a weapon enchant), so it no longer competes with a weapon imbue: a rogue keeps both poisons and still receives it (the sim/leveling kit gives the rogue specs Deadly Poison in the main hand and Instant Poison in the off hand, the arrangement that measured stronger than two Instants or either Deadly alone in design/reviews/2026-10-07-rogue-parity.md), and a dual wielder carries a stone in each hand. Since Blizzard's 10 November 2026 hotfix (Weapon imbues and Weapon totems can now be used at the same time) a shaman keeps its own Windfury Weapon and receives the totem as well. Paladins and shamans are on both factions in Forever, so the blessings and the totems reach either faction's raid entry. Nothing from Ahn'Qiraj or Naxxramas is used. The tanks (warrior-protection, paladin-protection, druid-feral-bear) share the tank consumable group, which adds armor, health, stamina and strength consumables in place of a damage dealer's; each carries one potion: Mighty Rage Potion for the warrior and the bear, a mana potion and then Major Spellblasting Potion for the paladin. Each tank also carries the main-hand imbue that measured best for its threat: an Elemental Sharpening Stone for the warrior and the bear, Brilliant Wizard Oil for the paladin (round 10). They are ranked against the curated boss and healers of data/curated/tank-encounter.json, and carry no Blessing of Salvation, which a tank does not want. Every tank's boss carries a raid warrior's Thunder Clap (debuffs_by_role), so a bear or paladin tank is judged against the same 20% slower boss a warrior tank is. Grace of Air Totem is left out: it is an air totem, so a party's shaman drops either it or Windfury Totem (the beta notes say the two do not stack), and Windfury measured 4 to 24% ahead of Grace of Air for every melee spec that can receive it (design/reviews/2026-10-08-remaining-trainables.md). Winter's Chill is left out: since client 1.60.1.70532 it is no longer a Frost crit debuff; its stacks raise only the applying mage's own next Cone of Cold, so a raid frost mage's stacks give no one else anything, and in the engine they would have fed this mage's Cone of Cold for free. Forever's foods give the stat of the Well Fed their aura 227 effect triggers, not Era's: Baked Salmon (28 spell damage) is the caster's and a paladin tank's food, Smoked Desert Dumplings (20 Strength) a strength user's and a warrior or bear tank's, and Poached Sunscale Salmon (40 attack power and ranged attack power) an agility user's (rounds 8 and 9, design/reviews/2026-11-02-sim-audit-round8/auras.md and design/reviews/2026-11-02-sim-audit-round9/auras.md). Where a slot lists two consumables the first one the character's level can use is carried, the spec's list before the class's before the group's, so a lower-level food follows the item it stands in for. Forever's 30-second potions share the two-minute potion category (4) with the mana and rage potions, so each spec carries the potion that measured best: Major Frenzy Potion for the rogues, the Survival hunter and Enhancement, Major Spellblasting Potion for Balance, Frost, Shadow and the paladin tank, the mana or rage potion for the rest (round 10). Their recipes are sold by the Azeroth Commerce Authority and Durotar Supply and Logistics alchemy vendors in Redridge Mountains and The Barrens. Forever lets a druid drink any potion and Thistle Tea in a form without leaving it, and weapon enchantments and Windfury Totem work in a form (the druid deep dive, news.blizzard.com article 24301515), so the cat carries the melee group's stone, Major Frenzy Potion and Thistle Tea, and Windfury Totem reaches the cat and the bear. The Blasted Lands buffs share one hour-long category (103), so each spec carries one: R.O.I.D.S. for strength users and tanks, Ground Scorpok Assay for rogues, hunters and Feral, Cerebral Cortex Compound for the damage casters and the Holy paladin and Restoration shaman, Gizzard Gum for the druid and priest healers (round 9).

buffs.label: Arcane Intellect
buffs.reason: Any Phase 1 raid has a mage; intellect for every mana user.

buffs.label: Mark of the Wild
buffs.reason: Any raid has a druid; all stats and armor. Plain version: Forever's Restoration tree has no Improved Mark of the Wild.

buffs.label: Power Word: Fortitude
buffs.reason: Any raid has a priest; stamina. Plain version: Forever's Discipline tree has no Improved Power Word: Fortitude.

buffs.label: Divine Spirit
buffs.reason: Spirit from a raid priest. In Forever it is a trainer spell (SkillLineAbility, Discipline, ranks at 30, 40, 50 and 60), not a talent, so every priest brings it.

buffs.label: Blessing of Might
buffs.reason: Attack power from a raid paladin. Plain version: Forever's Holy tree has no Improved Blessing of Might.

buffs.label: Blessing of Wisdom
buffs.reason: Mana per five seconds from a raid paladin. Plain version: no improved form in the live trees.

buffs.label: Battle Shout
buffs.reason: Attack power from a raid warrior. Plain version: Forever's warrior trees have no Improved Battle Shout.

buffs.label: Trueshot Aura
buffs.reason: Ranged attack power only (aura 124, 100 at 60 since the server hotfix push of 3 November 2026, which doubled rank 5 from 50; Forever dropped the melee half) from a raid hunter, a Marksmanship talent that exists in the live tree.

buffs.label: Heart of the Lion
buffs.reason: Any Phase 1 raid has a hunter. The client's area aura (spell 409583, sent every 14 seconds by the hunter's own Heart of the Lion, 409580) gives every ally within 100 yards, the whole raid and not only the party, 10% to every stat and 40 plus 4 per level above 1 melee and ranged attack power (280 at 60: 40 + 4 x 60, Wowhead Forever's tooltip reads 280). A hunter in the raid sets it anyway; the entry is what every other class receives.

buffs.label: Leader of the Pack
buffs.reason: 3% crit of every kind (aura 290) from a raid feral druid, a talent that exists in the live tree. Exclusive with Moonkin Aura since Blizzard's Forever notes of 3 November 2026, so a raid with both gives 3% once.

buffs.label: Moonkin Aura
buffs.reason: 3% crit of every kind (aura 290) from a raid balance druid; the live Balance tree has Moonkin Form. Exclusive with Leader of the Pack (Blizzard, 3 November 2026): the preset keeps both druids, and the engine gives 3% once.

buffs.label: Strength of Earth Totem
buffs.reason: Strength from a raid shaman. Plain version: the live shaman trees have no Enhancing Totems.

buffs.label: Windfury Totem
buffs.reason: In the 1.60 client the totem (spells 8512, 10613, 10614) is an aura on every party member that gives each main-hand hit a 20% chance of one extra attack with 246 extra attack power at rank 3, not a weapon enchant (only the shaman's own Windfury Weapon is), so it stacks with a poison or a sharpening stone on the weapon. A shaman with Windfury Weapon on the main hand does not receive it. The totem's aura (8515, 10609, 10612) has no duration: it ends with the totem, with none of vanilla's 10-second linger.

buffs.label: Mana Spring Totem
buffs.reason: Mana per five seconds from a raid Restoration shaman, improved: Restorative Totems (16187, Restoration tier 3, live in the 70707 tree; forever-bugs #215) adds 25% to Mana Spring at 5/5, and the Restoration shaman's raid build takes all five points (round 11).

debuffs.label: Curse of the Elements
debuffs.reason: Forever's all-magic curse, which the engine carries now; a raid warlock keeps it up.

debuffs.label: Sunder Armor
debuffs.reason: Five stacks, the engine applies them with its own periodic application; every raid warrior or druid brings it.

debuffs.label: Judgement of Wisdom
debuffs.reason: Mana returns from a raid paladin.

debuffs.label: Judgement of the Crusader
debuffs.reason: Holy damage taken from a raid paladin, who keeps it up on the boss (owner ruling, 2026-11-01). A level-60 paladin judges rank 6 (Seal of the Crusader 20308, learned at 52), whose Judgement 20303 adds 161 Holy damage taken in the Forever client (SpellEffect aura 14; Era's was 140). Plain version: the live trees have no Improved Seal of the Crusader.

debuffs.label: Judgement of Light
debuffs.reason: Health returns from a raid paladin; no damage effect, listed because a raid carries it.

debuffs.label: Hunter's Mark
debuffs.reason: Ranged attack power from a raid hunter. Plain version: the live Marksmanship tree has no Improved Hunter's Mark.

debuffs.label: Curse of Recklessness
debuffs.reason: Armor reduction from a raid warlock.

tank.label: Thunder Clap
tank.reason: A raid warrior keeps Thunder Clap on the boss whoever tanks (owner ruling, 2026-11-13), as it keeps Sunder Armor: rank 6 (11581), aura 319 at -20 in the client, 20% longer between the boss's swings. Only the tank is swung at, so only the tanks carry it. It is the same aura as a warrior tank's own Thunder Clap (one label, one exclusive attack-speed slot in the engine), so it never stacks with it: the warrior tank keeps the 20%, and its own clap no longer has a slow to keep up. Demoralizing Shout stays the tank's own.

ids.reason: A drink that makes the healer well fed with healing power; client level 45 (item 249870, spell 1249925). Nightfin Soup, the caster's meal, gives spell damage and is no use to a healer.

ids.label: Brilliant Mana Oil
ids.reason: Mana per five seconds and healing power on the main hand; client level 45. The engine states the client's amounts for the three mana oils.

ids.label: Major Mana Potion
ids.reason: Drunk by the engine's major-cooldown pass (the rotation's autocast line) whenever the bar has room for it and the two-minute cooldown is up; client level 49.

ids.label: Demonic Rune
ids.reason: Used by the engine's major-cooldown pass (the rotation's autocast line) whenever the bar has room for it and the two-minute cooldown is up, in the engine's conjured slot; it is the mana rune the engine models.

ids.label: Flask of Natural Aggression
ids.reason: Forever's Alchemy flask (item 274274, client level 55): 30 Stamina and 2% crit in Mount Hyjal, Hyjal Summit and the Barrow Deeps (the 1.60.1.70790 server push 113570 values). The best Natural flask for most melee and within 1% of the best for the rest (Precision for Retribution and Assassination, Accuracy for Arms), against no flask before.

ids.label: Elixir of the Mongoose
ids.reason: Agility and crit; client level 46.

ids.label: Juju Power
ids.reason: Strength: 30 (spell 16323). Elixir of Giants is item 9206 in the Forever client, renamed Elixir of Greater Strength, at 25 Strength (spell 11405), so Juju Power is the stronger of the engine's two strength elixirs (round 10).

ids.label: R.O.I.D.S.
ids.reason: Strength.

ids.label: Juju Might
ids.reason: Attack power. It shares the engine's attack-power slot with Winterfall Firewater and is the stronger of the two.

ids.label: Elemental Sharpening Stone
ids.reason: Main-hand stone for every melee weapon user, now that Windfury Totem is a raid buff and no longer holds the main-hand imbue slot. An enhancement shaman's Windfury Weapon still wins the slot. A feral druid carries it too: Forever's weapon enchantments work in a form (the druid deep dive), and it measured about 1.8% more damage for the cat (round 10). A rogue keeps the stone beside its poison: Forever lets a stone and a poison share a weapon (the rogue and warlock Deep Dive, 2026-10-07), and the sim carries it in the hand's stone field. Elemental (crit) on the main hand because the engine adds its 2% crit to the whole character, so a second one would count twice.

ids.label: Dense Sharpening Stone
ids.reason: The main hand's stone from level 35 until the Elemental Sharpening Stone at 50: 8 weapon damage (item 12404, or Dense Weightstone 12643 on a blunt weapon, the same 8; client level 35). The off hand already carries it from 35 (round 11).

dual_wield_ids.label: Dense Sharpening Stone
dual_wield_ids.reason: Off-hand stone for dual wielders: weapon damage, since the main hand already carries the one Elemental stone that counts.

ids.label: Flask of Natural Aggression
ids.reason: 30 Stamina and 2% crit in the Barrow Deeps and Hyjal (item 274274, client level 55). The best Natural flask for Beast Mastery and Marksmanship; Survival gains slightly more from Precision.

ids.label: Elixir of the Mongoose
ids.reason: Agility and crit; client level 46.

ids.label: Poached Sunscale Salmon

ids.label: Juju Might

ids.label: Flask of Natural Precision

ids.label: Elixir of Fortitude

ids.label: Rumsey Rum Black Label

ids.reason: Strength from the Blasted Lands (item 8410, 25 Strength, an hour): 1.2 to 1.8% more threat for all three tanks, ahead of Ground Scorpok Assay and Lung Juice Cocktail (round 9).

ids.label: Juju Might
